messages:
maria: kicking off canary for model v4 -> v4.1 at 10% traffic. added a cost guard: max_cost_per_minute=1200 tokens-equiv and latency p95 < 350ms. can someone eyeball the guard config before I let it run for an hour?

deploy-bot: started rollout 10% -> v4.1 on route /generate (canary id=canary-1769504321) :rocket:

ashley: quick note — user prompts for search-extract can spike tokens; last week a single customer caused a 3x token spike for 12m. if guard uses absolute tokens/min it might flap.

jon: agree. two suggestions: 1) use rolling p95 of tokens-per-request *and* median requests per minute; 2) require min_samples=50 in the window so tiny traffic doesn't trigger a pause.

kevin: also consider action softness. instead of immediate full "pause", we could first cut canary to 1% or route to a cheaper quantized variant. pause is too noisy.

linda: console UX request: when an automatic pause happens, show the exact metric + window + sample count and a link to the raw time-series and sample traces. teams keep opening tickets asking "why it paused".

maria: good points. proposal: guard config with hysteresis & tiered action. example config below — can we converge on semantics?

maria: ```json
{
  "guard_id": "cost-latency-guard-1",
  "metric": "cost_per_minute_equiv",
  "op": ">",
  "threshold": 1200,
  "window_sec": 300,
  "min_samples": 75,
  "consecutive_windows": 2,
  "hysteresis_pct": 0.15,
  "actions": [
    {"type": "throttle", "target_pct": 50},
    {"type": "route_fallback", "variant": "v4.1-quantized"},
    {"type": "pause", "min_duration_sec": 600}
  ]
}
```

ashley: love consecutive_windows. ensures transient blips don't kill canaries. hysteresis will prevent flip-flop. can we make actions conditional on sample counts? e.g., only pause if sample_count > 200.

jon: yea add "min_samples_for_pause" or let action have a "require": {"min_samples": 200}. Also add a backoff schedule: 10m -> 30m -> 60m pause escalation.

kevin: telemetry: we need a new metric: "canary_violation_rate" (per-minute) and include contextual fields: route, model_version, cost_bucket. that will simplify dashboards and alerts.

linda: +1 for an obvious audit trail. console should show who manually overrode, reason, and time window. also an "undo override" for 5 mins.

sre-ops: from runbook POV: alerts for first violation (pager? maybe not) should go to #eng-platform-alerts with runbook link. if a guard escalates to pause, create incident with small context blob (guard config id, last 3 windows, sample histogram).

maria: question: what do we do about A/B tests vs canary? A/B traffic splits will have small cohorts — min_samples will need to be lower. maybe guard should be scoped to rollout.kind (canary|ab) and have different thresholds.

jon: yep. add "scope": {"kind": "ab", "min_samples": 30, "action":"throttle"} sample. default canary stricter.

ashley: also, cost normalization. instead of raw cost we should compute "expected_cost" = sum(request_tokens * token_cost_model) across samples; guard compares ratio observed/expected > 1.3. that protects against seasonal prompt-length changes if cost model shifts.

maria: agree on normalization. also we need to persist the guard decisions to a central table for postmortem and ML-feature generation.

deploy-bot: guard "cost-latency-guard-1" detected violation: window_end=1769504560 samples=88 p95_latency=420ms cost_per_min=1350 -> action: throttle to 50% for canary (applied).

kevin: good, throttle first. can we emit a brief log line to the app logs so ops can correlate with customer errors? something like: "canary_guard: id=..., action=throttle, reason=cost, samples=88"

sre-ops: log format + runbook link would be great. also attach a small sample set of traces (one per shard) to the incident so teams can triage without jumping into console.

linda: UX follow-ups: 1) show guard timeline on rollout detail page, 2) allow filtering rollouts by guard state (paused/throttled/healthy), 3) expose effective action and how much traffic changed (absolute requests/min).

maria: next steps: I'll update the internal spec with hysteresis, sample gating for pause, and tiered actions. jon/ashley can you draft the minimal API changes to accept action-level requires? linda can you sketch the console UI copy for the paused state?

jon: will do a PR for API changes. thinking of small change: actions[] can include optional "requires" object.

ashley: I'll add the normalization math and tests for token spike scenarios.

linda: I'll mock the UI and include the log/trace link pattern.

deploy-bot: update: throttle ended (after 5m), rollback to 10% canary achieved. no pause triggered.

maria: awesome. let's ship the spec by EOD and get a follow-up thread after implementation. thanks all :clap:
